title: Aluminium chain

chokepoint.physics: Hall–Héroult runs non-stop; a potline freezes solid if power drops — one big unit at cheap power

deck: Bauxite is mined in three places at once — Australia, Guinea and China. But turning it into metal is one of the most electricity-hungry industrial processes there is, so the smelter, not the mine, is the chokepoint — and it went where power was cheapest.
byline: bauxite (spread) ≠ alumina ≠ smelting (electricity) ≠ the metal's carbon footprint
correction: A bauxite map looks diversified — Australia, Guinea and China each mine about a quarter. But aluminium smelting is ~40% electricity by cost, so it concentrated wherever power was cheap. China's share jumps from ~21% at the mine to ~59% at the smelter.

sections.h2: 1 · The mine is spread; the smelter is not

panels.note: USGS. The single most important number in this chain: China mines about a fifth of world bauxite but smelts nearly three-fifths of the metal. The concentration is built in the smelter, not the ground.

panels.text: Bauxite is abundant and heavy, so it is mined near many deposits. But smelting bauxite-derived alumina into metal is electrolysis at industrial scale — the single biggest cost is power. Smelters are therefore built where electricity is cheap and reliable, and over two decades that meant China's coal fleet, plus hydro in Canada, Norway and the Gulf's gas.
panels.flag: the chokepoint is the powerline, not the pit

panels.text: the electricity to smelt one tonne of primary aluminium — roughly what an average home uses in a year, per tonne of metal. Because power is such a large share of cost, the aluminium map is really an electricity map: it shows where cheap power was built.
panels.note: USGS: newer plants ~12 MWh/t, older ~15 MWh/t.

panels.text: Recycled (secondary) aluminium needs only about 5% of the electricity of primary smelting, so scrap is a huge, growing part of supply and a genuine relief valve — the metal is infinitely recyclable and worth recovering. As with PGMs, the above-ground stock cushions the mine-and-smelter chokepoint.

sections.h2: 3 · The carbon twist: same metal, very different footprint

panels.h3: How the world's smelters are powered
panels.note: International Aluminium Institute (IAI), latest fuel-mix statistics. Aluminium smelting draws roughly three-fifths of its electricity from COAL worldwide — the single reason the metal's carbon footprint is so power-dependent. China's own smelter fleet is close to 90% coal-fired, while Canada, Norway and Iceland run on hydro. (Figures are IAI industry aggregates, read off their fuel-mix dashboard.)

panels.text: the IAI global-average cradle-to-gate greenhouse-gas intensity of a tonne of primary aluminium — but the average hides everything. Hydro-powered metal sits near ~4 t CO₂e/t; coal-powered metal runs past ~20 t. Same metal, a 5× spread, set almost entirely by the smelter's powerline.
panels.note: IAI GHG-intensity statistics; hydro–coal range is IAI-consistent.

panels.text: Because smelting is electricity, a tonne of aluminium's carbon footprint depends almost entirely on the smelter's power source. Chinese coal-powered metal carries several times the CO₂ of hydro-powered metal from Canada, Norway or Iceland. 'Green aluminium' commands a premium, and carbon border adjustments (EU CBAM) turn the power source into a trade variable.
panels.flag: the power source is now a trade variable

panels.h3: The ore is moving even as the smelter stays
panels.text: Guinea holds the world's largest bauxite reserves and its exports to China are climbing, while Indonesia banned raw bauxite exports to force domestic refining. So the upstream is re-sorting — more Guinean ore, more Indonesian alumina — but the electricity-bound smelting chokepoint has not moved with it. Ore geography and smelter geography are two different maps.

trade_intro: BACI shows bauxite, alumina and unwrought-aluminium trade, but not smelter power sources or captive integration. Unwrought-aluminium trade also routes through metal hubs. Read exporter shares as availability of the traded form, not the smelting map.
